title: FSD S2 reads ACE views and the ALS, COLLINS, NLEADS and CCMS systems directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read ACE
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05 and DP-13
section: A2.5 integration points, A2.6 integration points and business rule R-SET-01, A2.10 integration points, A2.13 integration points, A2.16 and A2.17
description: The payoff and the settlement range are calculated 'from ALS' (R-SET-01), the collateral and encumbrance checks name 'ACE collateral views (v_ace_collateral, v_ace_collateral_detail; CCMS ingested by ACE)' and the Land Office, the plan is booked to NLEADS and ALS, and the collateral is released in CCMS. Architecture v5 slide 37 changes '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' to 'views read only by rwb-source-data', slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE's data' with rwb-source-data alone and adds that everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity, and the connection matrix on slide 13 gives the S2 row a Temporal call to P7, an event subscription from S8, Temporal calls to P5 and P8 and one Nexus operation to ACE Common, with no REST cell to P1. The Ownership Map records no view and no P1 path as this service's. The whole read path the offer rests on is therefore undefined in the FSD.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.6.3.1 (R-SET-01 'Calculate the payoff from ALS and set the range from reference data'), A2.13.2 (integration points 'ACE collateral views ...; CCMS ingested by ACE; Land Office'), A2.10.2 (integration points 'NLEADS, ALS and GL'), A2.17.2 (integration points 'CCMS, ALS and GL'). Arch v5 slide 37 (views read only by rwb-source-data), slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views; everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity), slide 13 (S2 row: T to P7, E from S8, T to P5, T and E to P8, N to ACE Common; no cell to P1). Rules DP-05, DP-13.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P1 owner
proposed: Obtain every source fact through the rwb-source-data contract and add the S2 to P1 REST cell to the connection matrix; this service reads no view and no ACE table, and a direct read fails the build and the boundary test.

title: The FSD returns the case to its prior status in COLLINS, and Architecture v5 gives COLLINS no path from this service
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 slides 16, 37 and 41; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 7
section: A2.9 Return the case to its prior status on no signature; A2.4 integration points
description: A2.9 sends the case back 'to the status it held in COLLINS' and names COLLINS as its integration point, and A2.4 names COLLINS, EFS, ACE and TDR. In Architecture v5 COLLINS is the collection system the case arrives from: source data lands through ACE ingestion, the interface configuration and the file runs belong to rwb-integration (slides 16 and 41), and no slide gives this service a COLLINS path. Who writes the prior status back, and on which interface, is not stated.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.9.1 ('Sends the case back to the status it held in COLLINS'), A2.9.2 integration points 'COLLINS, Workbench', A2.9.3.1 (R-RES-17, R-RES-18 'Moves to RETURNED_TO_COLLINS'), A2.4.2 integration points 'COLLINS, EFS, ACE and TDR'. Arch v5 slide 41 (P2 owns interface config, file runs, outbound items), slide 16 (P2 IN/OUT), slide 37 (source data through ACE ingestion). Rules DP-16.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Hold the prior status on the treatment and raise the write back to the collections system through the rwb-integration contract; P2 owns the interface, its retries and its exception queue.

title: The Ownership Map lists one table for rwb-treatment, although Architecture v5 gives it four entity groups
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 30 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables
section: Service contract, rwb-treatment, DB line
description: Arch v5 slide 41 states that rwb-treatment owns 'treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers', slide 18 states that it 'writes schema rwb_treatment: treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers', and slide 30 lists rwb_treatment among the 19 schemas. The Ownership Map tables sheet holds 93 rows and one of them is this service's: `treatment`. The contracts, the agreements and the plan timers have no register row, so the service that the architecture gives a schema has one table in the register that every story's data section is written from.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 (S2 rwb-treatment: owns treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers), slide 18 (DB writes schema rwb_treatment), slide 30 (19 recovery schemas). Ownership Map Tables: treatment, owner S2; no row for contracts, agreements or plan timers.
proposed: State the four entity groups and their key fields as product requirements and fix no physical table name; the table set and the physical schema are written when the S2 DB story is picked up, and the missing rows are added to the Ownership Map in the same change.

title: The offer command is named differently on the architecture slide and in the map, and the list operation of slide 18 has no row
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints; Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.7 and A2.8
section: A2.7 Send the offer and start the validity timer; A2.8 Route the signed offer to operations for booking
description: Arch v5 slide 18 names the IN operations as 'REST GET/POST /treatments; POST /treatments/{id}/offer'. The Ownership Map records POST /cases/{caseId}/treatments, GET /treatments/{treatmentId}, PATCH /treatments/{treatmentId} and POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit as this service's operations from API Specification v4 and TSD S2 appendix T-A. No GET /treatments list and no /offer path is in the map, so the command the screen calls and the read the treatment list needs are not agreed between the two sources.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (IN: REST GET/POST /treatments; POST /treatments/{id}/offer). Ownership Map Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/treatments, GET /treatments/{treatmentId}, PATCH /treatments/{treatmentId}, POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit, all owner S2; no GET /treatments and no /offer row. FSD S2 A2.7.2 and A2.8.2 integration points 'Workbench'.
proposed: Publish the command as the map's POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit and read slide 18's POST /treatments/{id}/offer as the same command; fix in the contract story whether a GET /treatments list is part of the contract before the screen is built.

title: TreatmentClosed has no event number and no row in the Ownership Map event sheet
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events
section: Service contract, rwb-treatment OUT
description: Arch v5 slide 18 gives rwb-treatment the OUT topic rwb.treatment.events.v1 with the events TreatmentApproved and TreatmentClosed, and slide 43 lists TreatmentApproved as row 10 (producer rwb-treatment, consumers rwb-comms and rwb-payment) and carries 'TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaim*' in the additional rows, produced by rwb-treatment or rwb-guarantee with rwb-case and rwb-reporting as consumers. The Ownership Map holds EV-10 TreatmentApproved only. The event this service publishes when a treatment closes therefore has no number, no producer and no consumer that can be tested.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (EVT rwb.treatment.events.v1: TreatmentApproved, TreatmentClosed), slide 43 row 10 (TreatmentApproved) and the additional row (TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaim*). Ownership Map Events: EV-10 owner S2; no TreatmentClosed row.
proposed: Publish TreatmentClosed on rwb.treatment.events.v1 keyed by caseId, CloudEvents, through the outbox, and carry it without an EV number until the catalogue allocates one; rwb-case and rwb-reporting consume it.

title: The plan timers are specified on the Workbench scheduler, which Architecture v5 replaces with durable timers
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-10
section: A2.10 Book the plan and set the schedule; A2.11 Detect and handle a broken plan; A2.7 the validity clock
description: A2.7 says the wait is 'a timer, not a routed state', A2.10 'starts the plan timers' and R-RES-25 moves the plan to running 'when first_due_date set', with 'Workbench' as the mechanism. Arch v5 slide 44 retires the shared Quartz tables in favour of a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service, rule DP-10 replaces Quartz and JOB-nn with the workflow kit, JOB-05 'timer check every 5 min' is recorded as retired to durable timers, and the Temporal design runs TreatmentWorkflow on rwb-treatment. The mechanism the FSD names for every clock in this module no longer exists.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.7.1 ('The wait is a timer, not a routed state'), A2.10.2 and A2.10.3.1 (R-RES-25). Arch v5 slide 44 (no shared Quartz tables; JOB-05 retired: timer inside the workflow), slide 20 (own task queue and its own Schedules). Temporal design slide 18 (TreatmentWorkflow, clocks: offer 14 days, settlement pay 30 days, credit approval 3 working days). Rules DP-10.
proposed: Set the validity, the credit approval and the plan clocks as durable timers inside TreatmentWorkflow through the workflow kit; no Quartz table, job or connection is used, and a breach is reported on the case timer path that rwb-case owns.

title: The FSD triggers on a completed ACE batch, and AceDataReady does not reach this service while no S2 job exists in the job map
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 43 and 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 jobs and events; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 6.3
description: Ten of the eighteen features state their trigger as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', which is the Workbench load model removed by D-RCV-35. In Architecture v5 the readiness signal is AceDataReady from rwb-source-data, consumed by rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation and rwb-writeoff; the job map holds JOB-01 to JOB-22 and none has owner S2. No source says what starts a treatment step when no case child is running, so the moment each of these steps runs is not fixed.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.1.2, A2.5.2, A2.6.2, A2.7.2, A2.9.2, A2.10.2, A2.11.2, A2.13.2, A2.16.2, A2.17.2, A2.18.2 step 1; A2.1.4.4 to A2.18.4.4 ('None, no background event'). Arch v5 slide 43 row 26 (AceDataReady consumers), slide 44 (job map; no S2 row). Program BRD v5 section 6.3 (the Workbench runs no inbound load). Ownership Map Jobs: no row with owner S2.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P1 owner
proposed: Run every step as a step of TreatmentWorkflow started by rwb-case, and by the events of the services that own the fact (TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed, the document and signature results); add no Schedule and no batch trigger to this service until the job map gives it one.

title: Booking, payment matching and posting are rwb-payment's in Architecture v5, while the FSD writes them from this module
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 jobs and events; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 section 3.8
section: A2.10 Book the plan and set the schedule; A2.11 Detect and handle a broken plan; A2.17 Release the collateral after settlement
description: A2.10 writes the plan to NLEADS and ALS, sets the payment schedule and starts the plan timers, A2.11 counts missed payments, and A2.17 tells CCMS to release the security. Architecture v5 gives rwb-payment the payment and proceeds matching, the fees and the bookings, with JOB-07 payment matching and JOB-08 booking confirmation as its event-triggered workflows, publishes TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched on rwb.payment.events.v1, and gives this service those three events as inputs. Two services therefore appear to write one booking.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.10.2 (integration points 'NLEADS, ALS and GL'), A2.11.2 ('ALS and GL, Workbench'), A2.17.2 ('CCMS, ALS and GL'). Arch v5 slide 41 (P8 owns payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings, posting files), slide 44 (JOB-07 and JOB-08 owner rwb-payment), slide 13 (S2 row: T and E to P8; P8 row: E from S2). Ownership Map Events: EV-11, EV-12 owner P8.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P8 owner
proposed: Record the booking reference from TreatmentBooked and the break from PaymentMissed, and let rwb-payment own the booking, the matching and the posting; the release request leaves through the integration contract and this service records the reference that returns.

title: The document set and the signature are rwb-document's and rwb-comms's in Architecture v5, while the FSD names the Workbench document hub
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 16 and 17; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 sections 3.5 and 3.6
section: A2.18 Generate the treatment document set; A2.8 the signed offer; A2.15 the inspection evidence
description: A2.18 generates the credit approval, the contract and the mortgage documents against 'the Workbench document hub' and A2.15 sends photographs, bills and checklists there, while A2.8 depends on a verified signature. Architecture v5 gives rwb-document the metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures and retention, gives rwb-comms the notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery with the e-signature request, and routes both across the module boundary: the map holds POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents and POST /documents/{documentId}/review as P5's and POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests as P6's, while the connection matrix gives the S2 row a Temporal call to P5 and no cell to P6 at all. The FSD's single 'document hub' integration point therefore hides two owning services, five operations and one missing call type.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.18.2 (integration points 'Workbench, the Workbench document hub'), A2.15.2 ('Field app, the Workbench document hub'), A2.8.3.1 (R-RES-16 'signature verified'). Arch v5 slide 41 (P5 and P6 ownership), slide 16 (P5 IN/OUT incl. POST /documents/generate), slide 17 (P6 IN/OUT), slide 13 (S2 row: T to P5; no cell to P6). Ownership Map Endpoints: the generated-documents, review, signature-request and signature-result rows.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P5 and P6 owners
proposed: Request generation, review and signature through the P5 and P6 contracts, hold the document reference on the treatment, and keep no document content in schema rwb_treatment.

title: The CCMS release, the Land Office title check and the asset take-on have no path from this service in Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 18, 19 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints
section: A2.12 Run a deed in lieu to ownership transfer; A2.13 Check encumbrance and eligibility; A2.17 Release the collateral after settlement
description: A2.12 records the asset in AMIS, settles the debt and releases the registration with CCMS, A2.13 checks title at the Land Office and plans a colour title search, and A2.17 tells CCMS to release the security. Architecture v5 gives rwb-asset the assets taken on, the holding and the floor price, gives rwb-integration the ACE integration paths and the outbound items, and gives this service, on slide 13, Temporal calls to P7, P5 and P8, an event subscription from S8 and one Nexus operation to ACE Common. Slide 19 gives rwb-asset the IN path for the asset record and the auction ladder. No cell carries a CCMS release, an AMIS record or a Land Office check from S2.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.12.3.1 (R-DIL-28 'Record the asset in AMIS, settle the debt and release the registration'), A2.13.2 (integration points incl. 'Land Office'), A2.17.3.1 (R-SET-20 'request the collateral release', R-DIL-27 'release the collateral in CCMS'). Arch v5 slide 41 (S5 asset, P2 integration), slide 19 (S5 IN/OUT), slide 13 (S2 row: no cell to S5, P2 or Outside).
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Request the asset take-on from S5 through its contract and the CCMS release and the title check through the rwb-integration contract, record the reference each returns, and add the two cells this service needs to the connection matrix.

title: The approval limits the settlement and deed in lieu depend on are held by another service, are open as a decision, and are quoted differently in two places
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables (delegation_limit); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 9 DL18; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 section 7 DL18
section: A2.3 Approve a settlement below the floor; A2.12 the deed below the floor
description: A2.3 routes a settlement below the floor 'to the approver or the committee named in the matrix' and A2.12 an R-DIL-15 second signature, without stating a limit. The Temporal design quotes the delegation twice: 'DoA 2.1.1: L6 <= THB 100m, 30% loss; L5 <= 150m; L4 <= 300m; L3 PARC <= 1,500m' in the slide and 'DoA 2.1.1 max loss: L6 30% / 50m; L5 35% / 75m; L4 45% / 150m; L3 PARC 45% / 750m' in its notes. The table that holds the limits is delegation_limit, owned by P4, and DL18 is open on the holders, the limits and the substitutes. The approval this module exists to take therefore has no agreed limit to test against.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.3.2 and A2.3.3.1 (R-SET-05), A2.12.3.1 (R-DIL-15). Temporal design slide 18 (DoA 2.1.1 amounts in the slide and in the notes). Ownership Map Tables: delegation_limit owner P4, ruling ASM-A6-tables-4. Program BRD v5 DL18; Epic 2 BRD v3 DL18 and section 7.1.
proposed: Read every limit from the versioned delegation table of rwb-access at run time, record the level applied and the approver role on the treatment, and test with one documented test set until DL18 is answered; the two quoted sets are not reconciled here.

title: Three Drools packages are named for this service with no code, version label or owner
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-04
section: A2.1, A2.2, A2.6 and A2.11 rule sections; the break rule and the matching rules
description: The Temporal design states 'S2 already has three Drools packages in Phase 1' and names RESTRUCTURE (R-RES-25/27/29/30/31, R-LIT-02), PAYMENT_MATCH (which replaces payment_match_rule, T10) and BOOKING_MATCH (booking confirmed), and records that the workflow mostly waits on offers, signatures and payments. No package code, version label, owner or registry row is given anywhere, and the Ownership Map gives the rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases to P7. The rules this module applies therefore have no governed package to evaluate.
evidence: Temporal design slide 18 ('S2 already has three Drools packages in Phase 1'), the Drools decides box and the notes (RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH, BOOKING_MATCH). Arch v5 slide 27 (authoring, approval and promotion in P7) and slide 41 (P7 owns the DMN model registry). Ownership Map Tables: rule_package and rule_package_version owner P7, ruling ASM-A6-tables-3.
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with P7
proposed: Evaluate the three packages from the embedded Drools kit with the universal rules in force, record the package and rule version on every treatment, and name the package codes, labels and owners in rwb-decision before wave 3 release.

title: The FSD acceptance criteria are placeholders, so no criterion of this module is observable as written
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.4.1 to A2.18.4.1
description: All eighteen main success criteria read 'AC-S2-0nn-01 | <feature name> | The data and rules it needs are in place | The trigger arrives | The result is recorded with its rule version | Written one epic ahead', and every alternate flow and system background event row reads 'None'. The exception rows are two boilerplate cases (a role without the right; a decision that cannot be recorded). No criterion states an amount, a state, a timer or a message, so no story of this module can be accepted against its source criterion and the criteria in this PRD are written from the FSD steps, rules and field catalog.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.1.4.1 to A2.18.4.1 (the eighteen rows quoted), A2.1.4.2 to A2.18.4.2 (None), A2.1.4.3 to A2.18.4.3 (two exception rows), A2.1.4.4 to A2.18.4.4 (None).
proposed: Keep every FSD AC ID as the evidence column and write each criterion from the FSD's own step, rule and field catalog; the FSD owner replaces the placeholders at the next FSD version, with the module's alternate flows and background events named.

title: The service is wave 2 and EP02 while every requirement of the module is an Epic 3 requirement
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 sections 5.9 and 8; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 sections 8.1 and 8.3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R5.6
section: Release sequencing of the module
description: Architecture v5 slide 41 and the rules give rwb-treatment wave 2, the Epic 2 BRD makes every one of its 32 requirements EP02 at wave 2 and releases Epic 2 on 31 December 2026 (tentative), and the FSD states the module's 'First in' as 'E2 foundations; E3' with all eighteen features at E3. The Program BRD places REQ-S2-001 to REQ-S2-010 in E3 and releases E3 on 31 January 2027 (tentative). One module is therefore created one release before the requirements it serves are released, and no source says which of its capabilities the E2 release carries.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 (S2 wave 2). Rules R5.6 (EP02 wave 2). Epic 2 BRD v3 sections 8.1 and 8.3 (S2 wave 2; EP02 wave 2; release 31 December 2026 (tentative)) and section 9 (every requirement EP02). FSD S2 document control ('E2 foundations; E3') and A1.2 (every feature first in E3). Program BRD v5 section 5.9 (Epic E3) and section 8 (E3 31 January 2027 (tentative)).
proposed: Publish the contract and deliver the treatment record with its data date in wave 2, and release the offer, settlement, plan and deed in lieu capabilities with E3; the split is stated in the release slicing of this PRD and changes no requirement.

title: Only one of the five messages this service shows is its own, and none has agreed wording
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 to A2.18 validation rules and exception flows; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 services; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 9 DL10
section: A2.1.3.1 to A2.18.3.1 validation rules; A2.1.4.3 to A2.18.4.3 exception flows
description: The FSD cites five message IDs: MSG-S2-001 ('The offer is below the floor of {floor}. It has been sent for approval.'), MSG-P1-001 for a stale data product, MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, MSG-P7-003 for a decision that cannot be recorded and MSG-GEN-001 for a required field. Four belong to other services, no message catalogue row is given for MSG-S2-001, and DL10 is open on the Thai name of every field, label and message. The wording a screen shows at an offer is therefore owned almost entirely outside this product.
evidence: FSD S2 VR-S2-001-1 to VR-S2-018-1 (MSG-S2-001, MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-001), A2.1.4.3 to A2.18.4.3 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003). Ownership Map Services: P1, P4 and P7 are the owners of the three services named. Program BRD v5 DL10; Epic 2 BRD v3 DL10.
proposed: Serve MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001 from the catalogues of the services that own them, hold MSG-S2-001 in this service's catalogue with a Thai and an English version, and put both through DL10 before wave 3 release.

title: The classification and the retention of the treatment, the agreements and the plan timers are not set
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-047, NFR-028 and DL26; Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) field catalog; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 section 7 DL26
description: NFR-047 requires a classification per data product and document type and states the scheme is to be applied; NFR-028 requires a retention class per document type with the periods not set; DL26 holds both open. The FSD marks all eight catalog fields as not personal data and gives no classification and no retention class for the treatment, the contracts, the settlement and deed in lieu agreements or the plan timers, which hold amounts that belong to a customer.
evidence: Program BRD v5 NFR-047, NFR-028 and DL26. Epic 2 BRD v3 section 7 DL26. FSD S2 A2.2.3.2 to A2.15.3.2 (Personal data: No for all eight fields).
proposed: Apply the working labels of this document (SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL for the terms and the agreements, CONFIDENTIAL for the references) and state the retention period as open; the class sets handling and the period is set under DL26.

title: The field catalog covers eight fields and none of them describes a contract, an agreement, a plan timer or a booking
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.2.3.2, A2.3.3.2, A2.4.3.2, A2.12.3.2, A2.15.3.2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41
section: A2.2 to A2.4 and A2.12 to A2.15 field catalog; the remaining features have none
description: The only field catalog in the FSD holds treatment.case_id, decision_log_id, treatment_type, proposed_by, proposed_at, offer_amount, haircut_amount and installments, and it is repeated in five features. Twelve of the eighteen features have no catalog at all, and no source gives a field for the contracts, the settlement and deed in lieu agreements, the plan timers, the booking reference, the inspection, the rental or the document set that Architecture v5 says the schema holds.
evidence: FSD S2 A2.2.3.2, A2.3.3.2, A2.4.3.2, A2.12.3.2, A2.15.3.2 (the same eight rows); A2.1, A2.5 to A2.11, A2.13, A2.14, A2.16 to A2.18 carry no field catalog. Arch v5 slide 18 and slide 41 (four entity groups).
proposed: Require the eight catalog fields as written and require the contract, the agreement, the plan timer and the booking reference to be held, leaving their physical field list open until the data architect writes it with the DB story.

title: The prerequisites of the module are feature codes of other modules that name no service
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.1 dependencies and A2.1.2 to A2.18.2 prerequisites; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 services
section: A1.1 Dependencies; the Prerequisites line of A2.1 to A2.18
description: The module's dependencies are written as FEAT-APD-01, FEAT-CHO-02, FEAT-CHO-06, FEAT-CHO-07, FEAT-CHO-08 (twice), FEAT-DCM-12, FEAT-OCC-01, FEAT-OCC-07, FEAT-OCC-09, FEAT-OCC-11, FEAT-TRT-04 and FEAT-VAL-06, and the same codes appear as the Prerequisites of individual features. The Ownership Map and the plan hold services, stories and legacy keys, not feature codes of other modules, so no dependency of this service can be resolved to a contract, a story or a team from the FSD as written.
evidence: FSD S2 A1.1 ('Dependencies. FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-CHO-02; FEAT-CHO-06; FEAT-CHO-07, FEAT-CHO-08; FEAT-CHO-08; FEAT-DCM-12; FEAT-OCC-01, FEAT-TRT-04; FEAT-OCC-07'), A2.1.2 to A2.18.2 prerequisites. Ownership Map Services and Endpoints (no feature codes).
proposed: Read each prerequisite as the contract of the service that owns the capability (approval to P7, case to P3, documents to P5, communications to P6, valuation to S1) and record the mapping once in the service contract; the duplicate FEAT-CHO-08 is carried as written.

title: No approval is recorded for the requirements this PRD states
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3 section 10.2; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 9; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R1 U8
section: Section 1 document control; Section 13 approval
description: The governing BRDs are at status Draft with an empty approval table (the Epic 2 BRD names its five approvers and records no decision), the run records no human verification stop (U8), and this document is written as Draft with an empty approval table. The requirements approval gate named in the playbook therefore has no recorded decision, and the PRD cannot claim one.
evidence: Epic 2 BRD v3 section 10.2 (approval table) and section 10.1 (Draft). Program BRD v5 (Draft, tool line of this run). Rules R1 U8 (no human verification stop in this run).
proposed: Keep the document at status Draft, leave the approval table empty, and treat the missing approval as an assumption rather than an answer; the gate is cleared by the Product Owner and the FDA after this run.

title: The history of FSD S2 versions 1 and 2 is not in the sources read, and the dependency sentence repeats a feature code
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control and A1.1
section: Document control; A1.1 Dependencies
description: FSD S2 is version 3 dated 15 November 2026 and its change note describes only the step from v2 to v3, stating that everything else is unchanged from v2. The dates and change notes of versions 1 and 2 are not in any source read. The A1.1 dependency sentence also names FEAT-CHO-08 twice, so the list as written cannot be counted.
evidence: FSD S2 document control (Version 3, Date 15 November 2026, Change note v3) with no version table; A1.1 ('FEAT-CHO-07, FEAT-CHO-08; FEAT-CHO-08').
proposed: Carry version 3 in full and mark versions 1 and 2 as not specified rather than reconstructing them, and read the repeated FEAT-CHO-08 as one dependency; the FSD owner supplies the two change notes at the next FSD version.

title: The treatment record exists twice: as this service's live record and as P1's dated copy
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables and rulings; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 41; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-013
section: Data ownership at the boundary between rwb-treatment and rwb-source-data
description: The Ownership Map gives `treatment` to S2 and `dp_treatment` to P1, and its ruling states that the live treatment and guarantee records stay with S2 and S3 while the dated DP04 copies stay with P1 as the data engine, built from events and read-only for reporting (ASM-A6-tables-14). Architecture v5 slide 37 removes the data lake and gives reporting to rwb-reporting. Two tables with one name therefore exist, and the row this service writes must not be read by this service from the copy.
evidence: Ownership Map Tables: treatment owner S2; dp_treatment owner P1 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-14. Arch v5 slide 18 and slide 41 (S2 owns the treatments), slide 37 (data lake removed). Program BRD v5 NFR-013.
proposed: Write only the live `treatment` row in schema rwb_treatment and read the dated copy only for reporting, never as the source of a treatment; the copy is P1's and built from this service's events.
